blocks.title: Search by meaning for every element of your node
blocks.description: Every element keeps its texts here as vectors and asks for the closest ones to a question, in any language. The meaning is counted on your own computer, with no key and no internet.

blocks.text: It names a collection and the text and sends them through the database element, the door every element already uses.
The node's own embeddings element turns the text into 384 numbers on this computer. Nothing leaves it.
The vector goes into its collection. A text with the same id replaces the old one.
A question is counted the same way and meets the closest texts of its own collection, each with its score.
A search reads only its own collection and only the nearest rows, then counts the exact score for them.

blocks.between: A search never crosses into another collection.

blocks.text: The deep memory keeps what each element was told in that element's collection: memory-said for the main agent, memory-said--<element> for an element.

A search touches only its own collection, so an element's question never meets another element's phrases. The main agent's question is asked in every collection, and the closest answers come together.
The collections divide the search. The store itself opens with the node's data key, and the computer it runs on is yours.
Every element of the node already has the database address and the data key. Store a text and find it again:

const base = process.env.REMOTE_DATA_URL
const headers = { 'X-Data-Secret': process.env.DATA_SECRET, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
await fetch(`${base}/vectors`, { method: 'POST', headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({ collection: 'faq', text: 'Delivery takes two days.', refTable: 'faq', refId: '17' }) })
const r = await fetch(`${base}/vectors/search`, { method: 'POST', headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({ collection: 'faq', query: 'How long is shipping?', k: 3 }) })
const { results } = await r.json() // [{ id, collection, refTable, refId, text, score }]
The answer lists the closest texts with their score. The same id replaces a text, and DELETE /vectors/:id removes it.
